summary.text: The Indian Ocean Dipole is an irregular swing in sea surface temperatures in which the western Indian Ocean becomes alternately warmer and then colder than the eastern part.
In its positive phase the west turns warm and wet while cooler eastern waters tend to bring drought to Indonesia and Australia, and the negative phase brings the opposite.
It interacts with El Niño–Southern Oscillation in the Pacific and affects monsoons over the Indian subcontinent, rainfall in south-east Australia and East Africa's short rains.

facts.label: Identified
facts.value: 1999, by Indian Institute of Science researchers

facts.label: Coral record
facts.value: Dipole index reaching back to 1846 AD

items.prompt: Forecasters announce a positive Indian Ocean Dipole for the coming months. What should farmers in south-east Australia expect?

options.label: Much heavier rain than usual
Rain well below average
No change from a normal year
Frequent tropical cyclones

items.explain: In the positive phase the winds that carry moisture across Australia weaken, so south-east rainfall falls well below average.

items.prompt: Researchers find that wind changes from an Indian Ocean Dipole event can produce El Niño-like warming in the Pacific. What does that show?

options.label: The dipole is just El Niño under another name
The Pacific controls the Indian Ocean but not the reverse
The two oceans' temperature swings are unrelated
Patterns in the Indian and Pacific Oceans interact

items.explain: The dipole interacts with ENSO, and dipole-driven wind anomalies can create El Niño-like temperature anomalies in the Pacific.

items.prompt: Water off northwest Australia turns unusually warm while the western Indian Ocean cools. What happens to rain in southern Australia?

options.label: It increases, carried in by moist winds
It drops sharply into drought
It shifts entirely to the north coast
It stays unaffected by the ocean

items.explain: In the negative phase, winds pick up moisture over the warm eastern water and sweep it toward southern Australia, bringing more rain.

items.prompt: Why is this climate pattern called a "dipole"?

options.label: It always lasts for exactly two years
It was found by two research teams at once
Two sides of the ocean swing opposite ways
It links the North and South Poles together

items.explain: The western Indian Ocean becomes alternately warmer and colder than the eastern part, so the two sides form opposite poles.

items.prompt: Climate change is expected to warm the western Indian Ocean faster than before. What does that suggest for East Africa's October–December short rains?

options.label: More intense rainfall in the short rains
Steadily weaker and drier short rains
Short rains that move to midsummer
No change, since the rains are set by land

items.explain: Faster western warming is expected to make positive dipole events more common, which is likely to intensify the short-rain season over East Africa.

items.prompt: At the end of 2019 a particularly strong positive dipole was under way. How did rainfall over East Africa compare with normal?

options.label: Far below normal, near drought
Close to a typical year
About 300% higher than normal
Somewhat lower than normal

items.explain: Average East African rainfall was 300% higher than normal, causing widespread flooding.
